title: GTM Engineering Working Student
description:
Companies have invested billions into ERP systems. And yet, most business decisions are still made the way they were in 1995: on fragmented data, manual exports, and Excel. Finance teams spend five to ten days every month copy-pasting numbers, and four systems show four versions of the same revenue.

AI changes that. At ARC, we are building the AI-native Finance OS: one platform that connects all of a company's systems, answers any question in seconds, finds errors before they cost millions, and automates reporting end to end. Leading Mittelstand companies like Burmester, Pfanner, and Ferrotec, and PE firms like AUCTUS and GENUI, already run their finance on ARC. Finance software is being rebuilt from the ground up this decade, and we intend to win the category.

We are a small, AI-native team in Berlin, fresh off our seed round led by 42CAP, growing revenue 10x since our pre-seed. We build, experiment, and move fast, take real ownership, and keep a low-ego culture.

Aufgaben

You are the GTM Engineering Intern at ARC. While our BDRs are on the phone with CFOs, you build the machine behind them: the automations, data pipelines, and AI workflows that decide who we call, with what message, and when. We sell an AI-native platform, so our own go-to-market has to run AI-native too. You'll build our internal GTM OS from the ground up.

What you'll do

  • Build automated prospecting pipelines: sourcing multi-entity Mittelstand groups and PE-backed companies that fit our ICP, at scale
  • Enrich accounts and contacts with the signals that matter to us: legal entities, ERP landscape, PE ownership, trigger events like ERP migrations or acquisitions
  • Automate outreach workflows across email, LinkedIn, and phone, and keep them personal enough that a German CFO actually responds
  • Connect and orchestrate our GTM stack (HubSpot, Aircall, enrichment and outreach tools) into one system with clean data flowing through it
  • Use AI models aggressively: for research, list building, message drafting, call analysis, and anything else that removes manual work from the pipeline
  • Build dashboards and KPI tracking so we always know what's working in outbound and what isn't
  • Prototype, test, and iterate: your experiments directly shape how ARC's GTM engine works as we scale the sales team

Qualifikation

What makes you a great fit

  • You love building things: with no-code tools, scripts, APIs, or AI agents, whatever gets it done fastest
  • You're deep in the modern AI tool stack and use LLMs daily as a matter of course
  • You're analytical and rigorous with data: messy lists and broken syncs bother you until they're fixed
  • You have strong business sense and can think from the prospect's perspective, not just the pipeline's
  • You're hands-on and not afraid of unglamorous work: cleaning a CRM included
  • You communicate well in English; German is a plus since our market is the German Mittelstand
  • You want to work with smart and friendly people with (self-reported) low ego
  • You want to work on-site 5 days a week in our new Berlin office

You may not be a good fit if

  • You need detailed instructions and shy away from taking responsibility
  • You're not willing to deeply understand the product and the buyer behind your automations
  • You're only interested in high-level "strategic" work
  • You think GTM engineering means setting up one Zapier flow
  • You've never built anything on your own initiative
  • You prefer working remotely
  • You prefer working with minimal collaboration
  • You want to work a 9-5 job

  • Attack Our Product: Pentest the ilert platform end to end — web app, public API, webhooks, and integrations. Hunt for what actually matters in multi-tenant SaaS: broken auth and authz, tenant isolation failures, IDOR, SSRF, injection, and abuse of our alerting and escalation logic.
  • Red Team Our Infrastructure: Probe our cloud and Kubernetes configuration, secrets handling, CI/CD pipelines, and software supply chain. Find the path from "small misconfiguration" to "real access."
  • Run Authorized Social Engineering: Design and run phishing and pretexting exercises against our own team — always under a written scope signed off by the CTO before you start, always debriefed as a learning exercise, never punitive. Then help us fix what the exercise exposed.
  • Break the AI, Too: We're building an AI SRE that investigates incidents and can execute actions on approval. Prompt injection, tool abuse, and agent-boundary testing are wide-open ground here — and largely unexplored.
  • Harden the SDLC: Bring dependency, secrets, and static analysis into CI where it earns its place. Threat-model new features with the engineers building them. Review the security-relevant PRs.
  • Write Findings People Can Act On: A reproducible proof of concept, an honest severity call, and a concrete fix — then pair with the engineer who ships it. We care as much about closing the gap as finding it.

Requirements

  • Current Student: Enrolled in Computer Science, IT Security, Informatics, or a related technical field.
  • Demonstrable Offensive Work: Not coursework or certificates — things you've actually done. CTF results, HackTheBox/TryHackMe progression, bug bounty reports, a home lab you built, a writeup you published, a CVE you found. Show us one and walk us through it.
  • You Can Read and Write Code: Enough to navigate a real codebase (we run Java, Rust, TypeScript/React), understand why a bug exists, and propose the fix — not just report that a scanner flagged something.
  • Web Security Fundamentals: OWASP Top 10 as a working tool, not a memorized list. Authentication and session handling, access control, injection classes, SSRF, and what makes multi-tenancy hard.
  • Comfortable With the Tooling: Burp Suite or equivalent, plus the usual recon and exploitation kit — and the judgment to know when manual beats automated.
  • Judgment and Discretion: This role comes with access and trust. You stay inside the agreed scope, you don't test things you weren't authorized to test, and you handle what you find responsibly. Non-negotiable.
  • Language: Fluent English (our working language).
  • Location: Able to be in our Cologne office regularly — the role is hybrid, not remote.

Bonus points

  • Cloud or Kubernetes security, Infrastructure-as-Code scanning
  • CI/CD and supply chain security (SAST, DAST, SCA, SBOM)
  • LLM and agent security — prompt injection, tool-use boundaries, agent sandboxing
  • Detection engineering: not just getting in, but noticing when someone else does
  • German language skills
  • A published CVE, security blog, meetup talk, or open source security tooling

Benefits

  • 🎯 A Real Attack Surface: Not a lab, not a CTF box. Production software that companies worldwide depend on during their worst moments.
  • 🧨 Build the Practice: You're the first security hire. What offensive security looks like at ilert is genuinely yours to define — with the CTO in your corner.

  • 🌴 Focus Culture: We protect maker time, favor async, and keep meetings rare.

We hire for talent and a builder's mentality, not a checklist. If you have a writeup, a CTF profile, a disclosed vulnerability, or a tool you built — bring it. That tells us more than any certification will.

description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

title: Immobilienmakler (m/w/d) – Schwerpunkt Vermietung | Werkstudent oder Teilzeit
description:
Warum LPE Immobilien?

  • Du wirst eingearbeitet, bevor du loslegst. Die ersten Wochen läufst du mit, schaust zu und übernimmst Schritt für Schritt. Erst wenn du sicher bist, bekommst du eigene Objekte — nicht am ersten Tag.
  • Du lernst den Markt an der schnellsten Stelle kennen. Vermietung ist der Bereich, in dem man am schnellsten versteht, wie Immobilien funktionieren: warum sich eine Wohnung in drei Tagen vermietet und die im selben Haus in sechs Wochen nicht.
  • Du sprichst selbst mit Kunden. Interessenten, Mieter, Eigentümer. Du bist vor Ort das Gesicht von LPE und nicht die Stimme im Hintergrund.
  • Du hast einen festen Ansprechpartner. Ein Makler aus dem Team begleitet dich, gibt dir Rückmeldung und übernimmt, wenn ein Fall komplizierter wird. Fragen zu stellen ist bei uns kein Zeichen von Schwäche, sondern Teil des Jobs.
  • Wir entwickeln unsere Makler selbst. Wer bei uns lernt und liefert, hat nach dem Studium eine Perspektive.
  • Du arbeitest mit Software, die es sonst nicht gibt. Unser eigenes System lpeOS bildet Prozesse ab, für die andere Unternehmen noch mit Excel-Listen und Papierordnern arbeiten.


Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine Aufgaben

  • Du organisierst die Vermarktung einer Einheit. Fototermin mit unseren Fotografen abstimmen und begleiten, Exposé erstellen, Inserat veröffentlichen und aktuell halten. Beim Exposé unterstützt dich unser Marketing.
  • Du kümmerst dich um die Interessenten. Anfragen sichten und vorqualifizieren, Termine koordinieren, Besichtigungen durchführen und nachfassen. Auch dann, wenn auf ein Objekt vierzig Anfragen kommen.
  • Du bereitest die Mieterauswahl vor. Unterlagen auf Vollständigkeit prüfen, Bonitätsnachweise sichten und deine Einschätzung zu den Bewerbern abgeben. Die finale Entscheidung trefft ihr gemeinsam.
  • Du unterstützt bei Abnahmen und Übergaben: Protokolle vorbereiten, Zählerstände erfassen, Mängel dokumentieren, Schlüssel übergeben.
  • Du hältst die Daten sauber. Jeder Kontakt, jeder Termin, jeder Status im System. Das klingt unspektakulär und ist die Grundlage dafür, dass bei uns nichts verloren geht.
  • Du arbeitest den Maklern zu. Termine vorbereiten, Objektunterlagen zusammenstellen, Korrespondenz übernehmen, bei Interessenten und Dienstleistern nachfassen. Vieles davon lernst du dabei nebenbei — weil du siehst, wie ein erfahrener Makler einen Fall aufbaut.
  • Du übernimmst Backoffice-Aufgaben. Stammdaten pflegen, Unterlagen digitalisieren und ablegen, Prozesse dokumentieren. Wie viel das ist, hängt von der Auslastung ab — planbar besprechen wir das jede Woche.


Was du mitbringen solltest

  • Du gehst offen auf Menschen zu. Eine Besichtigung mit acht fremden Leuten zu führen, muss dir liegen. Perfekt sein musst du dabei am Anfang nicht.
  • Du hast ein Gespür für Menschen — oder willst es entwickeln. Bei der Mieterauswahl zählt nicht nur die Bonität, und genau dieses Urteil lernst du bei uns.
  • Du bist gut organisiert. Mehrere Objekte, Termine und Fristen parallel: Wer hier den Überblick verliert, verliert auch den guten Mieter.
  • Du arbeitest zuverlässig. Interessenten stehen sonst vor verschlossener Tür, und das kostet uns beim Eigentümer mehr als jeder Fehler im Exposé.
  • Du fragst nach, statt zu raten — bei Kunden genauso wie im Team.
  • Du bist eingeschrieben oder suchst eine Teilzeitstelle. Die Studienrichtung ist zweitrangig, kaufmännisches oder immobilienwirtschaftliches Interesse hilft.
  • Du lernst Software schnell und denkst digital.

Vorerfahrung in der Immobilienbranche brauchst du nicht. Das Handwerk bringen wir dir bei.


Was wir dir bieten

  • Einarbeitung. Du läufst mit, bekommst deine Aufgaben schrittweise und arbeitest ab dem ersten Tag mit jemandem zusammen, den du alles fragen kannst.
  • Aufgaben, die dich weiterbringen. Du machst keine Ablage und keine Kaffeeküche, sondern Arbeit, die im Lebenslauf etwas bedeutet und die du im nächsten Bewerbungsgespräch erklären kannst.
  • Perspektive nach dem Studium. Wer bei uns lernt und liefert, bekommt eine Zukunft und nicht nur ein Zeugnis.
  • Persönliche Weiterentwicklung. Wohin du dich entwickeln willst, besprechen wir offen und regelmäßig — und wir sorgen dafür, dass du die Aufgaben und die Unterstützung bekommst, die dich dorthin bringen.
  • Gelebte Feedback-Kultur. Feedback ist das schnellste Werkzeug, das wir haben, um besser zu werden. Deshalb geben wir es sofort und nicht einmal im Jahr. Das gilt in beide Richtungen: Du bekommst ehrliche Rückmeldung — und wir erwarten sie genauso von dir.
  • Planbarkeit im Semester. Vorlesungszeiten und Klausurphasen stimmen wir im Voraus ab, statt sie zum Problem zu machen. Besichtigungen liegen ohnehin häufig am späten Nachmittag.
  • Modernste Ausstattung: Premium-Hardware, cloudbasierte Tools, papierlos.
  • e-Mobilität inklusive: internes E-Carsharing für Termine und private Erledigungen.

title: Staff Engineer (m|w|d) - CRM Tech
description:
Reliable data, resilient services and scalable architectures are at the heart of every CRM interaction at idealo. As a Staff Engineer, you'll shape the technical foundation behind identity resolution, subscriptions, data flows, and message delivery while ensuring GDPR compliance and supporting personalized user experiences.

This role combines backend engineering, data engineering and architectural leadership. You'll influence how data flows across systems, how services communicate through event-driven architectures, and how technical decisions support idealo's long-term CRM strategy. Working closely with Software Engineers, Data Engineers and Product Managers, you'll help define technical direction across multiple domains.

You'll work with Java, Spring Boot, Kafka, Braze, Snowflake and AWS services including Glue, Lambda and S3 in a modern cloud-native architecture. From data ingestion and transformation to customer-facing activation, you'll help build reliable systems that teams across idealo depend on every day. When new CRM capabilities go live, you'll see the direct impact of your work in millions of customer interactions.

The position is available in full or part-time.

About your new role

  • Design, implement, maintain, and evolve reliable and scalable software systems and data flows for CRM and user engagement use cases.  

  • Stay hands-on by designing and developing cloud-native microservices, event-driven applications and backend services with a strong focus on performance, security and operational excellence.

  • Lead technical initiatives within and across the team to align technical solutions with business needs.

  • Drive continuous improvements across software development, CI/CD pipelines, cloud infrastructure, observability, and monitoring while evaluating new technologies where they add measurable value.

  • Mentor engineers through technical guidance, architecture discussions and code reviews, fostering a collaborative engineering culture focused on sustainable technical excellence.


Skills & Requirements

  • You bring extensive experience building cloud-native software systems on AWS and designing distributed, event-driven architectures using Java 17+, Spring Boot, Kafka and modern backend technologies.

description:
nuuEnergy - Das sind WIR!

Unsere Mission: Wir bringen die Wärmewende in die Zukunft und bauen ein System für lokale Handwerks-Betriebe, das Qualität und Effizienz vereint. Das ist nicht einfach und viele sind hier schon gescheitert – bei Qualität, bei Kultur, bei Prozessen. Aber wenn wir diese Challenge meistern, gestalten wir die Zukunft einer ganzen Branche.

Konkret heißt das: Wir entwickeln das Betriebssystem für unsere Wärmepumpen-Standorte deutschlandweit — von Prozessen, über Kundenakquise und Handwerker-Hiring bis hin zu unserer eigenen Software.

Deine Aufgaben

Als Senior Venture Architect baust du die Strukturen und Systeme, mit denen nuuEnergy skaliert, und steuerst die Unternehmensentwicklung. Aktuell heißt das vor allem: Du bringst unsere Standortleiter zum Laufen. Das heißt du führst sie nicht nur, sondern baust die Systeme, mit denen sie eigenständig performen. Darüber hinaus bist du der unternehmerische Arm der Gründer: Du übernimmst, wo es noch keinen klaren Owner gibt, triffst Entscheidungen im Auftrag der Geschäftsführung und arbeitest cross-funktional mit allen anderen Leads. Kein Verwalter-Job, sondern ein Gestalter-Job.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Standortmodell zum Laufen bringen: ein wiederholbares Modell bauen, mit dem Hubs eigenständig, wirtschaftlich und menschlich stark laufen.
  • Standortleiter zu echten Unternehmern vor Ort entwickeln: technisch starke Menschen bei Führung und Organisation coachen, Konflikte in Handwerksteams lösen und Standards durchsetzen, ohne die Teams zu entmündigen.
  • Wichtige Sonderprojekte schnell von 0 auf 1 bringen und neue Geschäftsmodelle mit Venture Builder Methoden testen & entwickeln.
  • Team- und Orga-Probleme eigenständig lösen (Ziel: der Großteil läuft ohne die Gründer).
  • Personalentscheidungen mittragen — inkl. Trennungen, wenn nötig.
  • A-Player-Quote im Team messbar machen und aktiv steuern.
  • Cross-funktional mit allen Leads relevante Business-Entscheidungen vorbereiten und im Auftrag der Geschäftsführung treffen.
  • Die Geschäftsführung in Meetings, gegenüber Team Leads und extern vertreten.


Dein Profil

  • Deutsch auf C2-Niveau und wohnhaft in München
  • Echte Startup-Erfahrung: Im Aufbau (z.B. Venture Building, Early Stage, Wachstums-Phase) – kein Corporate-Hintergrund.
  • Führungserfahrung: Menschen geführt, aufgebaut und auch harte Personalentscheidungen getroffen.
  • Builder Mindset: Du bist Generalist/in und baust lieber Systeme, als sie zu verwalten.
  • KPI-fokussiert: Du steuerst mit Zahlen, nicht mit Bauchgefühl.
  • Persönlichkeit: Hungrig, hohe Arbeitsbereitschaft, Lust auf Aufbauen unter Unsicherheit.
  • Mobilität: Reisebereitschaft zu unseren Standorten.
  • Branchenerfahrung: Wärmepumpen, Energie, Handwerk, Bau oder dezentrale Servicemodelle (Logistik, Retail, Franchise etc.).


Was dich bei uns erwartet

title: Senior Finance Manager (all genders)
description:
Your role

About FRASER 

FRASER is an independent creative agency with teams across Berlin, Zurich, Cape Town and Dubai. We develop integrated campaigns, content and digital experiences for ambitious international brands, combining strategic thinking, creativity and technology. As we continue to grow, we're building scalable operations to support our international business. 

 Your role 

  • Take ownership of the finance function across FRASER, ensuring accurate financial reporting and efficient day-to-day financial operations.  
  • Prepare monthly management accounts, budgets, cash flow forecasts and financial analyses to support business decisions.  
  • Oversee accounts payable, accounts receivable, banking, payment runs, reconciliations and liquidity planning.  
  • Coordinate the preparation of bookkeeping (Vorbereitende Buchhaltung), ensuring invoices, purchase orders and supporting documentation are complete and accurate before submission to external accounting partners. 
  • Work closely with our external accounting firms in Germany, Switzerland, South Africa and Dubai, ensuring smooth collaboration and timely financial processes. 
  • Coordinate month-end and year-end closing activities together with external accountants and tax advisors.  
  • Ensure compliance with German accounting, tax and statutory requirements while supporting finance processes across our international locations.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Customer Success Manager

🌍 About us

Plinth is a fast-growing tech startup working with charities, foundations and local government. Small and local charities are highly effective but largely hidden. They have no spare time and no spare money. We're building the tools these organisations need and shining a light on the work they do. Read more on our blog.

🚀We're growing fast. 3-4x this year. We get 7+ new clients a month and we're shipping new features every few days. This means things move quickly and your work directly shapes how we scale. You'll have real responsibility from day one.

❤️It's really impactful work. Our clients are charities and grassroots organisations across the UK, and soon internationally. When you help them succeed with our platform, you're directly amplifying their impact. Every successful onboarding means a charity spends less time fighting with their systems and more time on their actual mission.

🤝You'll work with impressive people. Our team is talented, collaborative and slightly strange(?). We value impact, speed and openness. We work in person in our office in Old Street because we genuinely enjoy each other's company (most of the time). It’s a high trust, creative space where if you think something's a good idea, you just go do it.

💼 You need to be able to:

  • Work both fast and slow: You'll navigate slow public sector procurement cycles one minute, then help us ship a new feature over lunch the next. The whiplash is intense but it keeps things interesting.

  • Keep it real: You'll be getting the train to community centres and youth clubs where the heating doesn't work and where the paint is peeling off the walls. It’s rarely glamourous. You need to be willing to meet clients where they are, literally and figuratively.

  • Listen to problems, ignore solutions: Clients will tell you exactly what they think they need. Your job is to understand the actual problem and guide them to what will really work, even when they're convinced they already know the answer. This requires self-confidence, understanding of the platform and genuine listening in equal measure.

  • Teach people: Most of our clients don't love shiny gadgets. If you're the kind of person who enjoys teaching your gran to use a smartphone, this is ideal. You need to explain some fairly complex systems clearly without being condescending and still getting user adoption

  • Automate and document yourself away:🤖 We're small and growing fast. Build systems and processes that make your job increasingly redundant. There’s always plenty more to do.

  • Understand the difference between "urgent" and 🚨 URGENT — When you're managing 4-8 concurrent client projects and everyone thinks their issue is critical, you need to distinguish between what must happen for launch versus what can wait. This is harder than it sounds.

  • Grow with the role: we need someone who is comfortable with our clients and team doubling every 6 months. Your role will rapidly change to reflect that, but it leaves you with lots of room to grow in responsibility.

🧩 What kind of background do we think would be a good fit?

We’d expect a few years experience in something like the following:

  • Coaching / Tutoring: You know how to meet people where they are and guide them to better outcomes

  • Hospitality management: Service mindset, de-escalation skills, managing expectations when things don't go to plan, letting the customer think they’re right when they aren’t

  • Event/production management: Used to juggling moving pieces, keeping stakeholders calm, making last-minute pivots when things go wrong

  • Community organising/activism: Already comfortable in the spaces you'll be visiting, get the mission, used to working with limited resources

  • Consulting: You're used to parachuting into chaos, extracting actionable tasks, and keeping multiple clients calm simultaneously

  • User research/UX: Good at understanding what people actually need versus what they say they need, synthesising feedback into actionable insights

  • Knowledge of the charity sector is a significant advantage, whether that’s as an employee, consultant or as a long term volunteer.

  • It would also definitely be helpful if you have any technical experience to help with managing data migrations.

Importantly, This is a list of suggestions.

If you have experience in only some of this, or have only some of these skills, please do apply anyway.

📈 How can you measure your success?

  • Speed of getting customers successfully using Plinth: From signed contract to actively using the platform and seeing value.

  • Positive recommendations: Clients recommending us positively to their networks — it’s a big source of our growth.

  • Increasing use of Plinth: Clients expanding how they use the platform over time, not just maintaining baseline usage

🧠 The role

Client Onboarding (70%) — Lead onboarding from kick-off to go-live. Break down complex projects into clear phases. Manage timelines, priorities, and expectations across 7+ new clients per month. Stay on top of new features we ship every few days. Push back when needed and teach anyone regardless of background.

Operations & Process Improvement (30%) — Audit and optimise our support systems (expect to manage Intercom chat a couple of days a week). Refine onboarding workflows. Keep documentation current. Work with engineering to communicate what's urgent versus what's just a problem. Track feature requests across clients and synthesise them into product improvements.

💵 What we offer

  • Salary: £42,000 - £75,000 depending on experience

  • Equity as part of your package

  • Location: In-person, Old Street, London

☎️ Interview process

  1. Quick (20-30 min) call with Chris as a sanity check

  2. First interview with Chris and a co-founder

  3. Long (2-3 hour), quite intense, in-person interview — meet the team, do tasks, respond to case studies, be challenged

  4. Decision

title: Operations Associate
description:
TLDR: Plinth builds software for charities, foundations and funders. 2,000+ UK organisations use us, we add 7+ clients a month, and we ship constantly. HR, security, legal and finance currently sit with one person. That stops working at our next size. We're hiring someone to own a chunk of it: recruitment operations, contracts and invoicing, and the paperwork behind our ISO 27001 certification. You don't need to have done security or legal work before. You need to be the kind of person who picks up something unfamiliar, works out how it should run, then runs it properly.

What you'll own

  • Recruitment operations. The pipeline end to end. Keeping our tools current, booking interviews, wrangling schedules, first-pass CV screening, and working with team leads to build the tasks candidates get set. Candidates never wait on us

  • Contracting and invoicing. Contracts out, chased, signed and filed. Invoices raised and paid. Unglamorous, and it matters that someone holds it

  • Security administration. We're going through ISO 27001 now, and keeping a certification is more work than getting one. Reviews on a schedule, evidence that has to exist, paperwork that has to be generated. You own that calendar and it doesn't slip

  • Security questionnaires. Customers send long ones and they hold up deals. You'll answer them with support from the team and our internal tooling, and build a reusable answer bank so the tenth takes an hour instead of a day. You don't need to be a security expert. You do need to be confident enough to learn out loud

  • Automating the repeatable bits. A lot of this job is the same task on a loop, and a lot of it shouldn't be. Doing something by hand for the tenth time is a bug you're responsible for. You'll build the templates, automations and AI workflows that take it off your plate, then move on to harder work

  • Making the role bigger. Ops is four functions and one and a half people. As we grow, you're first in line for whatever you've shown you can hold

title: Talent Lead (6-month FTC)
description:
About Odin

Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.

 

We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

 

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

 

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

 

Mission

As we prepare to scale and launch in the US, you will bring immediate senior hiring capacity into Odin to close the priority leadership and high-impact roles for Q3 and Q4.

 

Responsibilities

Reporting to Imani, our Head of People & Talent;

  • Drive the end-to-end hiring process for priority leadership and L3+ (Senior) roles, ensuring momentum, clarity, and consistent progress from kick-off to offer

  • Take full ownership of pipelines, market mapping, outbound sourcing, and candidate management for critical roles across Product, Engineering, Sales, Design, Ops, and Finance

  • Maintain structured scorecards, ensure interview feedback is timely and high quality, and support wash-ups and calibration discussions

  • Conduct thoughtful qualification calls, assessing both skills and values alignment

  • Set a high trust, human candidate experience from first touchpoint through to decision

  • Partner with hiring team in role kick-offs to turn vague or early-stage ideas into clear, aligned role definitions with crisp expectations, level, and impact areas

  • Ensure all processes begin with a grounded understanding of what “great” looks like

 

By the end of the 6 month FTC you will have partnered with the team to deliver 4–5 leadership or senior high-impact hires. We may extend the contract depending on priorities.

 

About You

  • You’re a thoughtful, experienced talent partner who cares deeply about people, process and outcomes, with strong internal filters and high standards

  • You’ve led multiple hiring processes at once, ideally in a fast-paced, early-stage environment where ambiguity, urgency and competing priorities are the norm

  • You have experience in talent operations and attention to detail – spotting blockers early, keeping things moving, and improving systems as you go

  • You’re a clear, intentional communicator across async, written and verbal channels – able to bring others with you and influence at a senior level

  • You lead confidently in ambiguity, surfacing risks, asking the right questions, and helping hiring managers move forward with aligned, quality decisions

  • You adjust your style depending on the stakeholder - balancing care with challenge, and using strategic empathy to support better thinking across the hiring team

  • You’ve got excellent hiring judgement across different functions – able to assess skills, behaviours and values alignment, not just experience on paper

  • You’re a strong sourcer who knows how to write compelling outreach and build genuine relationships with passive candidates

  • You hold high standards for candidate experience and treat people with care, even when things are moving quickly

  • You’re curious and improvement-minded - always looking for ways to make the process better, and not afraid to challenge existing norms

  • You’re calm and clear under pressure, with strong follow-through and a focus on reducing complexity

  • You take ownership for both outcomes and experience - leading processes that others can rely on, and helping us build a better hiring culture along the way

 

This role is probably not a fit if you..

  • Struggle to challenge or influence senior stakeholders – A strong candidate should be able to push back constructively, challenge thinking when needed, and drive clarity – even in rooms with senior leaders.

  • Don’t enjoy outbound work - This role requires proactive pipeline building.

  • Play back opinions rather than surfacing original thinking – We need someone who brings their own views to the table, not just someone who agrees or repeats what’s already been said.

  • Over-focuses on the what rather than the how – Someone who takes things at face value, struggles to read between the lines, or doesn’t think critically about context won’t thrive. This role requires someone who can interrogate the brief, challenge assumptions, and make sense of what’s not said as much as what is.

 

Bottom line

This isn’t about whether you’ve done 360 hiring before - it’s about how you approach it.

We’re not looking for someone to simply execute. We’re hiring a strategic partner who thinks deeply about the role hiring plays in a business, asks the right questions, and isn’t afraid to challenge when needed. You’ll be the first person every candidate meets and a key influence on how managers shape their thinking. You’re not just moving people through a process - you’re holding the bar, shaping the experience, and carrying our values at every step.

 

Salary

The salary band for this 6 month FTC is £75,000 to £100,000 pro rata. The range is intentionally broad to reflect different levels of seniority and experience.

 

Location

This role can be remote, although we work regularly from our London office and would love someone who is open to spending some initial time with us in person for onboarding. For candidates who can do a hybrid setup, we’re in the office three days a week.

 

Working at Odin

We're a fast-growing startup building something very ambitious, and we expect you to work hard and relish this challenge. However, we also offer flexibility and support your life outside of work so you can bring your best to the table.

Our benefits include:

  • Work from anywhere for up to 6 weeks a year

  • Private health insurance, paid sick leave (including support for pregnancy loss and fertility treatments), and free access to Spill for mental health support

  • 4% pension employer contribution, with salary sacrifice options and NI savings reinvested into your pension

  • 25 days of annual leave (pro-rata), 2 wellness days, and flexible bank holidays

  • An extra day off to celebrate your birthday

Compensation: £75K – £100K

title: Chief of Staff
description:
JOB SUMMARY

More in Common is looking for a Chief of Staff.  This is a new role and a rare opportunity to help shape the next phase of a fast-growing global organisation working on some of the most urgent issues of our time, working at the CEO's side with a unique vantage point across our country teams, strategy and network of funders and partners worldwide.
(Please note that the preferred London location is for ease of communication with Tim Dixon, who is based in the UK. The postholder will not be involved in the day-to-day polling and research activities of More in Common UK, and will not report or routinely provide support to our Executive Director in the UK, Luke Tryl.)


ABOUT MORE IN COMMON

More in Common is a nonprofit dedicated to understanding the dynamics of polarisation, and identifying solutions that can strengthen social cohesion and confidence in democracy. We help leaders navigate the dynamics of polarisation more effectively, find common ground and bring people together to address shared challenges. More in Common's work is frequently featured in media and used by leaders in government, nonprofits, philanthropy, education, the arts and business. 
 
We have a country-led model, with work deeply rooted in national contexts and led by country directors in each of our seven countries, with a total headcount approaching 100. Our teams generate research insights, translate them into thought leadership, and disseminate and implement them across a wide ecosystem of partners and stakeholders. We hold relationships with leaders in many sectors of society, across politics, media, business, civil society, philanthropy, culture and faith, and from national leaders to local community groups. Recent work has produced fresh insights into public attitudes on immigration, online safety, nature and the energy transition, Ukraine, and democracy.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

This is a rare opportunity to help shape the next phase of a fast-growing global organisation working on some of the most urgent issues of our time, working at the CEO's side with a unique vantage point across our country teams, strategy and network of funders and partners worldwide. 
 
The Chief of Staff is a new role, created as More in Common transitions from its founding phase, when the organisation was led by its co-founders, to sole CEO leadership. It incorporates a senior adviser role, in which the Chief of Staff will be the principal aide, advisor and coordinator to the global CEO Tim Dixon, ensuring priorities advance, decisions move efficiently and commitments are executed. The Chief of Staff will also act as organisational glue: working closely with More in Common’s team of country leaders and directors, ensuring alignment between country executive directors, the global team and the CEO around More in Common's strategy, programmes and operations, and helping spot and resolve problems before they escalate.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategy

  • Strategic counsel: Trusted thought partner to the CEO on strategy and major decisions, drawing on visibility across the whole organisation and ensuring alignment within its country-led model. 
  • CEO communications: Shapes the CEO’s internal and external communications, and absorbs the coordination, communication, and follow-through work that would otherwise pull the CEO away from key public-facing responsibilities.
 
Organisational coordination
  • CEO workflow: Manages the CEO's priorities, time and decision pipeline with the Senior Executive Coordinator, so the right issues get attention and decisions don't stall. 
  • Team alignment and delivery: Keeps global and country teams aligned on shared priorities, facilitates decision-making across the organisation, and leads special projects requiring senior-level attention.
 
Leadership 
  • Country ED support: Liaises with country Executive Directors on the CEO's behalf, identifying where teams need more support and providing assistance in crises. 
  • Talent and succession: Supports leadership succession planning and mentors emerging leaders across country teams.


QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

We are looking for a candidate with:

  • Commitment to More in Common’s mission and values.
  • Experience working closely with, or in direct support of, a senior executive, founder or CEO.
  • Exceptional organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders and time-sensitive decisions simultaneously. 
  • Sound judgement and discretion, including experience handling sensitive or confidential matters. 
  • Comfortable operating with incomplete information, and confident making calls on when to resolve issues independently versus escalate. 
  • The ability to lead through influence rather than authority, working effectively with peers and country teams who have their own mandates and priorities.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to synthesise complex information for diverse audiences.
  • Inter-disciplinary interests and experience, such as having worked in different sectors (business, government, nonprofit), countries and roles. 
  • Fluency in English and at least one of French, German, Spanish, Polish or Portuguese languages.
  • At least six years’ working experience in such fields as public opinion research, public policy, political science, and international relations.


OTHER INFORMATION

More in Common intentionally invests time, energy, and resources in nurturing a distinctive values-driven culture. This culture defines how we work together as a team and with others:

  • Humble, ambitious and generous
  • Rigour and excellence in everything we do
  • Driven by the common good, not by ideology or partisanship
  • Deep curiosity about people, and a commitment to elevating others’ views, particularly those whose voices are largely unheard
  • Firmly rooted in each of our national contexts but curious about the world beyond
  • Valuing diversity of thought, allowing our own beliefs to be challenged and embracing healthy disagreement
  • Embracing a dual role as both sense-makers and change-makers
  • Valuing courage and risk-taking
  • Embracing learning and innovation, and always looking for new paths to make a difference
  • Engaging others from a starting point of trust
  • Drawing from a wide range of backgrounds, worldviews, identities and life experiences
  • Believing in the power of a good laugh and being a great place to work.


COMPENSATION AND CONDITIONS

  • Competitive salary related to location, and excellent benefits along with generous leave and family policy 
  • Some regular international travel
  • Personal learning budget
  • Working in one of our country offices, with a preference for London as our CEO is most often there


DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION
